gloss: ear; give ear, listen; (another older root) scales, weigh
summary: The ear, as a part of the body and as the organ of hearing, and the hiphil verb made from it, “give ear”. Words spoken “in the ears of” someone are spoken in his hearing; to incline the ear is to attend, to uncover the ear is to reveal, and Yahweh, who planted the ear, gives ear to prayer and opens the ear of his servant to obey. The scales מֹאזְנַיִם and the piel “weigh” share the spelling only: Arabic wazana, Ugaritic mznm and scripture's own Aramaic מֹאזַנְיָא show a root wzn with z, where the ear shows ḏ (Arabic ʾuḏun, Aramaic ʾudnā).

words.summary: About 187 times, mostly dual אָזְנַיִם. Set beside the eye as the two senses Yahweh made (Pro 20:12; Psa 94:9), and beside the heart, which understands what the ear hears (Isa 6:10; Pro 2:2).

senses.definition: The ear itself: its lobe touched with blood at the consecration of the priests and the cleansing of a leper, pierced with an awl for a servant who would not go free, hung with rings, or cut off.

evidence.note: Blood put “on the lobe of the right ear (אֹזֶן) of Aaron and his sons”.
The same at the cleansing of a leper.
His master “shall bore his ear (אָזְנוֹ) through with an awl, and he shall serve him for ever”.
“The rings that were in their ears.”
“Rings on your ears.”
“Your nose and your ears they will cut off.”
The shepherd rescues from the lion's mouth “two legs or a piece of an ear”.

senses.gloss: ear, as the organ of hearing; hearing
senses.definition: The ear that hears, tests words and receives instruction; ears that do not hear are the mark of idols and of a people who will not understand.

evidence.note: “He who planted the ear (אֹזֶן), does he not hear? He who formed the eye, does he not see?”
“The hearing ear and the seeing eye, Yahweh has made them both.”
“Does not the ear test words as the palate tastes food?”
“The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.”
“By the hearing of the ear I had heard of you, but now my eye sees you.”
Idols: “they have ears but do not hear”.
“Who have eyes and do not see, who have ears and do not hear”; taken up in Mrk 8:18.
“Make their ears heavy … lest they hear with their ears and understand with their heart”; quoted in Mat 13:15 and Act 28:27.
“Yahweh has not given you … ears to hear, to this day”; quoted in Rom 11:8.
“The ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.”
“The ear of the wise seeks knowledge.”
“A wise reprover on a listening ear.”
“Having ears, do you not hear?”
“Blessed are your ears, because they hear.”
“He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”
“What eye has not seen and ear has not heard”, from Isa 64:3.

senses.gloss: in the ears of: in the hearing of
senses.definition: With בְּ, words are spoken, read or set “in the ears of” someone: openly, so that they hear them.

evidence.note: Ephron answered Abraham “in the ears of the sons of Heth, of all who went in at the gate of his city”.
“Let your servant speak a word in my lord's ears.”
He took the book of the covenant “and read in the ears of the people”.
Moses spoke the words of the song “in the ears of all the assembly of Israel”.
Josiah read “in their ears all the words of the book of the covenant”.
Baruch reads the scroll “in the ears of the people”.
“The ears of all the people were to the book of the law.”
“Write this … and set it in the ears of Joshua.”
The people complained “in the ears of Yahweh”.
“As you have spoken in my ears, so I will do to you.”
“In my ears, Yahweh of armies”: what Yahweh has heard and sworn.
The cries of the harvesters “have entered the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth”.

senses.definition: To incline (הִטָּה) or give the ear is to attend; Yahweh is asked to incline his ear to prayer, and Israel is blamed because it would not incline its ear to the prophets.

evidence.note: “Incline, Yahweh, your ear and hear; open, Yahweh, your eyes and see.”
“Because he inclined his ear to me, I will call on him all my days.”
“Let your ear be attentive and your eyes open.”
“The eyes of Yahweh are toward the righteous, and his ears toward their cry”; quoted in 1Pe 3:12.
“They did not listen or incline their ear, but walked in their own counsels.”
“My son, attend to my words; incline your ear to my sayings.”
“He who turns away his ear from hearing the law, even his prayer is an abomination.”
“Nor his ear heavy, that it cannot hear.”
“They made their ears heavy from hearing.”

senses.gloss: uncover, open the ear: reveal, teach
senses.definition: To uncover (גָּלָה) someone's ear is to tell him what he did not know; Yahweh uncovers or opens the ear to reveal his purpose, to instruct, and to make his servant obey.

evidence.note: “Yahweh had uncovered the ear of Samuel a day before Saul came, saying …”
“My father does nothing great or small without uncovering my ear.”
Boaz: “I thought to uncover your ear, saying, Buy it.”
“You, Yahweh of armies, have uncovered the ear of your servant, saying, I will build you a house.”
God “uncovers the ear of men and seals their instruction”.
“He wakens my ear to hear as disciples … Adonai Yahweh has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious.”
“Sacrifice and offering you did not desire; ears you have dug for me”; Heb 10:5–9 reads the psalm of Christ.

senses.definition: Of news of judgment so dreadful that every ear that hears it tingles.

evidence.note: “I am doing a thing in Israel at which both ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.”

evidence.locator: Gen.20.8, Gen.23.13, Gen.23.16, אֹזֶן → οὖς; οὖς renders אֹזֶן ×136

evidence.note: Isa 6:10: “with their ears (ὠσίν) they have heard heavily.”
Jer 5:21 and Ezk 12:2.
Psa 34:16: “his ears (ὦτα) toward their prayer.”
The ear of the high priest's servant, cut off.

parallels.note: The eye, set beside the ear as the other sense Yahweh made; seeing and hearing go together.
The heart, which understands what the ear hears.

evidence.note: “Making your ear attend to wisdom, inclining your heart to understanding.”

phrases.gloss: in the ears of: in the hearing of

words.summary: Made from the noun: to lend the ear. Hiphil only, 41 times, nearly all in poetry and prophecy, and most often beside שָׁמַע “hear” or the hiphil of קָשַׁב “attend”.

stems.gloss: give ear, listen; give ear to prayer; heed

senses.definition: The summons to hear what is about to be said: to a family, a people, the nations, or heaven and earth called as witnesses.

evidence.note: “Give ear (הַאֲזִינוּ), heavens, and I will speak; and let the earth hear (תִשְׁמַע) the words of my mouth.”
“Hear, heavens, and give ear, earth, for Yahweh has spoken.”
Lamech: “Hear my voice … give ear to my word.”
“Hear this, all peoples; give ear, all inhabitants of the world.”
“Give ear, my people, to my law; incline your ears to the words of my mouth.”
“Hear this, priests; attend, house of Israel; give ear, house of the king.”
“I gave ear to your reasonings.”
Peter: “Give ear (ἐνωτίσασθε) to my words.”

senses.definition: Of Yahweh: to listen to one who calls on him, and so to answer.

evidence.note: “My voice to God, and I cry out; my voice to God, and he gave ear to me.”
“Yahweh did not hear your voice nor give ear to you.”
“If I called and he answered me, I would not believe that he gave ear to my voice.”

senses.definition: To listen so as to do: Yahweh's commandments, his prophets; or, of the wicked, to heed wicked lips.

evidence.note: “If you will diligently hear the voice of Yahweh … and give ear to his commandments and keep all his statutes.”
“You testified against them by your spirit by your prophets, but they would not give ear.”
“An evildoer heeds wicked lips.”
Idols' ears do not give ear.
“From of old they have not heard, not given ear … no eye has seen a God besides you”; taken up in 1Co 2:9.
Its one New Testament use: Peter's call to the men of Judea.

parallels.note: “Hear”: the fixed partner of הַאֲזִין in the summons to listen.

words.summary: Fifteen times, always dual: the pair of pans in which silver and goods are weighed. Its cognates show a root wzn “weigh” with z behind ז, not the ḏ of the ear; the Hebrew spelling with א joins it to אזנ.

senses.definition: The balance in which silver, hair or dust is weighed.

evidence.note: “I weighed the silver in the scales (בְּמֹאזְנָיִם).”
“Take scales for weighing and divide the hair.”
“Weighed the mountains in a פֶּלֶס and the hills in scales.”
“The nations … counted as dust on the scales.”

senses.definition: Scales of righteousness or of deceit: honest weight in trade, which Yahweh commands and owns, against the false scales he hates.

evidence.note: “Scales of righteousness, weights of righteousness … I am Yahweh your God.”
“A balance and scales of justice are Yahweh's; all the weights of the bag are his work.”
“Scales of deceit are an abomination to Yahweh, but a full weight is his delight.”

senses.gloss: weighed in the scales: tried, judged
senses.definition: A man or his trouble weighed in the scales, and found heavy or wanting.

evidence.note: “Let him weigh me in scales of righteousness, and God will know my integrity.”
“Sons of men are a lie; in the scales they go up; together they are lighter than breath.”
The rider on the black horse “having a balance (ζυγόν) in his hand”.

parallels.note: A balance or level, beside the scales.

words.summary: Scripture's Aramaic, once. It is spelled with ז, where Aramaic writes ד for the ḏ of the ear (אֻדְנָא): the Aramaic itself shows that the scales are not the ear's root.

senses.definition: The scales in which God weighed Belshazzar and found him wanting.

evidence.note: “תְּקֵל: you have been weighed in the scales (בְמֹאזַנְיָא) and found wanting.”

words.summary: Once, of Qoheleth. Read with the scales, “weigh” (as Arabic wazana and Ge'ez mazzana); the context, with “search out” and “set in order” proverbs, fits weighing his words, though “give ear” cannot be ruled out.

senses.definition: To weigh sayings, as on scales, before setting them in order.

evidence.note: “He taught the people knowledge, וְאִזֵּן וְחִקֵּר: he weighed and searched out and set in order many proverbs.”

words.summary: Once, in the camp law: a peg or spade is to be “with your אָזֵן”. Its link to the root is not clear. The ear's handle sense in Arabic, Syriac and Akkadian, and Akkadian uzuntu “ring or attachment on implements”, suggest something that hangs from a belt or weapon, but no verse fixes it.

senses.definition: What a soldier carries, to which a digging peg is added.

evidence.note: “You shall have a peg (יָתֵד) with (עַל) your אֲזֵנֶךָ, and when you sit outside you shall dig with it.”
“The ear; one of the organs of sense.”

cognates.gloss: give ear, listen to; (form IV) make known, announce
cognates.note: A verb from the ear, as the Hebrew hiphil is: listening, and making to hear.

evidence.note: “He gave ear or listened to it.”
“A making known; a notification; an announcement.”

cognates.note: Akkadian writes z for both ḏ and z, so it shows nothing of the merged letter; its “attention, understanding” is the ear that hears and heeds.

evidence.locator: SEM000509 uḏn [ear] N, AKK014461 uznu [ear] N

cognates.note: Ugaritic writes d here for older ḏ.

evidence.locator: SEM000509 uḏn [ear] N, UGC000106 udn [ear] N

cognates.note: Aramaic writes d for older ḏ, so the ear is ʾdn in Syriac; the Peshitta's word for the ears of Mat 13:15 and Mrk 8:18.
Jewish Aramaic: the Targums render אֹזֶן by it at Isa 64:3, Psa 18:45, Exo 29:20 and Deu 29:3.

evidence.locator: s.v. אוֹדֶן, אוּדְנָא (A00568), citing Targ. Is. LXIV, 3; Targ. Ps. XVIII, 45; Targ. Ex. XXIX, 20; Targ. Deut. XXIX, 3
SEM000509 uḏn [ear] N, GEZ000695 ʾəzn [ear] N

cognates.gloss: weigh, be of full weight; (mīzān) balance, pair of scales
cognates.note: Arabic z, not ḏ: the scales are a root wzn, apart from the ear. מֹאזְנַיִם answers to mīzān, a noun of instrument from wzn.

evidence.note: “A weighing-instrument; a balance; a pair of scales.”
A dual of *מוֹזֵן from ו־ז־ן “weigh”, compared with Arabic وَزَنَ.

cognates.note: Written with z, where the ear is udn: Ugaritic keeps the two roots apart.
Neo-Assyrian, three times; an “ear” of a tool. Could explain אָזֵן as something attached to a soldier's gear.

evidence.locator: armep x000120060, uzuntu [ring or attachment on implements] N

doctrine.statement: The psalmist reasons from the ear to its maker: “He who planted the ear, does he not hear?” (Psa 94:9). Yahweh's ears are toward the cry of the righteous (Psa 34:16, taken up in 1Pe 3:12), and his ear is not too heavy to hear; what keeps him from hearing is iniquity (Isa 59:1–2), and the prayer of one who turns his ear from the law is an abomination (Pro 28:9). So the faithful ask him to incline his ear (2Ki 19:16; Psa 86:1), and he gives ear (Psa 77:2): the God who hears is the God whose word is heard.

Yahweh's servant says, “Adonai Yahweh has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious”; morning by morning he wakens his ear to hear as one taught (Isa 50:4–5). Psa 40:7–9 sets the ear Yahweh dug against sacrifice: “I delight to do your will.” Hebrews reads that psalm of Christ, whose doing of God's will takes the place of the sacrifices (Heb 10:5–10), and says that he learned obedience from what he suffered (Heb 5:8). The Son was a man taught by his Father through the opened ear, and his obedience was learned, not assumed.

Ears that do not hear belong to idols (Psa 115:6) and to a people who will not understand (Jer 5:21); Isaiah was sent to make the people's ears heavy “lest they hear with their ears and understand with their heart, and turn and be healed” (Isa 6:10). Jesus quoted the verse of those who heard his parables without understanding (Mat 13:13–15), and Paul of those in Rome who would not believe (Act 28:25–28). Hence “he who has ears to hear, let him hear” (Mat 13:9): hearing that counts is hearing that understands and turns.

note: Two older roots in one spelling: the ear and its hiphil verb show ḏ (Arabic ʾuḏun, Ugaritic udn, Aramaic and Syriac ʾdn); the scales and the piel of Ecc 12:9 show z (Arabic wazana/mīzān, Ugaritic mznm, Ge'ez mazzana, and Biblical Aramaic מֹאזַנְיָא with ז). Hebrew מֹאזְנַיִם is then *mawzan- with an א spelling. Is Ecc 12:9 'weigh' or 'give ear'? Filed with the scales; check. אָזֵן (Deu 23:14) has no cognate sharing its meaning; Akkadian uzuntu is only possible. Proper names: Jaazaniah, Azaniah and Ozni have name files (jaazaniah, azaniah, ozni). Place names left without entries: אַזְנוֹת תָּבוֹר (a.cg.ah, Jos 19:34, perhaps 'ears' = peaks of Tabor) and אֻזֵּן שֶׁאֱרָה (a.ch.ac, 1Ch 7:24); the a.cg.ah tokens in the brief are mis-filed תָּבוֹר. Egyptian jdn 'ear' (TLA tla34070) is a possible, irregular relation through Afroasiatic, not a loan, so not recorded. Arabic أَذِنَ also 'permit' (إِذْن) and أَذَان the call to prayer: not followed. Ge'ez forms are from the Proto-Semitic list only; check Dillmann/Leslau pages.
